name: DEEP SPACE V2 (now with LESS NOISE)
summary: Various graphical tweaks to turn this into No Child's Sky
author: ProjectPatrick
description:
The philosophy is contrast and immersion, there can be no dark if everything is light, no vibrancy if everything is colorful. Everyone wants sugar until they are sick.

This mod removes:
Chromatic Aberration
Scanlines
Depth of Field
Vignette (Including faux-Binocular vignette)

This mod tweaks:
Version 1.
-Global Color (Much less red)
-Space Color (Very Dark)
-Rim Lighting (Lowers, Does not remove)
-Nebulaes (They are now subtle)
-Clouds (Little more transparent and less Super Mario 64 white puffs)
-Cloud Noise Textures (Higher Resolution)
-Warp (Feel the gods pulling you to your destination, gently.)
-LOD (Level of Detail)
Version 2.
-Sky Noise (Lowered Greatly, clear night skies boys.)
-Distant Planet Colors (they are their natural color when gazing through the night)
-Warp/Pulse/Boost/Space Lines (Reduced and tweaked, not removed)
-Dual Compasses Removed :^)
-Rim Lighting (Reduced Further)
-Landscape Fog (Reduced)

name: Gek Building retext
summary: Last part of my Aliens building overhaul
author: ScavangeR
description:
My third and last part of Aliens building retext: Gek Buildings !
Since this race is the Tradding one, I make the choice to go for something really "pimp" and radically different of the vanilla. Hope
you'll like it !

This mod "overlap" a part of my Landpad one but landpad is still mendatory to get full retext.

Actually the game use the same textures for all landpads + Gek buildings wich kinda annoy me.

Anyway, I realy think those textures are working fine but if you have any change suggestion, let me know because I took "risks" with that marble thing :D

INSTALLATION:
Choose a version:
- Main one with goldish exteriors but overlaping ALL my landpads retextures
- "Geks_arnt_pimps" for rusty looking and not overlaping my landpads retextures
unzip in c:/.../No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS

For MOAR retexture, check my other mod

name: JJs Better Ships
summary: Removes C class from ships and makes S class ships common.
author: JJhookah
description:
JJs Better Ships
[color=#00ff00]Version 5.3[/color]
Author[color=#00ff00] [color=#f4f4f4]JJhookah[/color]
[/color]

                                                                      [color=#00ff00]Updated for Swarm 6.43[/color]
                                                                 See below for Version changes.

Removes C class and makes S Class ships as common as other ships.
All ships types are still available but will be S, A and B class only.
                              
[color=#ffff00]Install[/color]
Step 1 : Extract from zip.
Step 2 : Open the extracted unzipped folder and copy the JJs.Better.Ships folder found inside to your No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder.
Create a Mods folder if you don't already have one.
Ensure mods are enabled in No Mans Sky / binaries / SETTINGS / GCMODSETTINGS.MXML :
<Property name="DisableAllMods" value="false" />

[color=#ffff00]Uninstall[/color]
Delete JJs.Better.Ships folder from No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS

Made with TubOcrisco's excellent NMS MODDING STATION.
[color=#00ff00]
Special Thanks again to Monkeyman192 for updating compilers.[/color]

Would also like to thank JovianStone for help locating a certain file.

Modifies: INVENTORYTABLE.MBIN
                 AISPACESHIPMANAGER.MBIN

Version 1.1 changes

Fixed shuttles, haulers, fighters, explorers and freighters not spawning in S class.

Thanks to Majora4613 for bringing this to my attention.
Also added optional "No Shuttles" version as suggested by Majora4613.
Please only use one version at a time.

Version 1.2 Changes

Added police ship and police freighters. {see new pics}
Made ambient freighter spawns warp in.
Added "warp in" Capital Freighters to secondary "warp in" fleet.
Increased possible size of secondary fleet spawn.

Version 1.2 uses above mentioned files plus: EXPERIENCESPAWNTABLE.MBIN
Uses different files to Redmas "Massive Fleet" but I would not recommend trying to use these two mods together.
Fully compatible with my "Planetary Freighters" mod.
Highly recommend using "No Blinding Freighters" by Lo2k.

Version 1.3 changes

Fixed issue of police ships spawning in place of fighters, especially in Vykeen systems.
[color=#00ff00]
V 1.4 NEXT[/color]

Updated for NEXT
For compatibility and functionality police ships and police freighters have been removed from mod.
Recruitable frigates are only available in ambient spawns  {All spawns that don't have capital freighters}
Recruitable frigates classes are unaffected by mod.

name: Better Planet Generation
summary: A huge planet generation overhaul that aims at making your hundreds of hours of exploration in the magnificent, infinite universe of No Man's Sky less repetitive and hopefully even more memorable.
author: WoodyMontana
description:
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][i][b]                                                     [size=6]Better Planet Generation[/size][/b][/i][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738968-1312445652.jpeg[/img]

[size=4][b]More planets

[/b][size=3]Better Planet Generation is a total overhaul of the planetary generation in No Man's Sky.[/size] [size=3]It improves by a significant margin the procedural aspect of the universe while at the same time respecting the original work and vision from Hello Games.[/size]

[size=3]It adds thousands of new distinct environments to the universe[/size][/size]. All of them come in five different life levels and varying placement scales and layouts. These environments were made to seamlessly combine with each other in many different ways.

Better Planet Generation is designed to bring variety to the different biomes you will visit but most of all it brings a lot of variation to the universe. Outside of the countless combinations of assets and their resulting new environments, planets you visit will present themselves differently each time. Placement layouts, scale of the regions, density, variety of assets and their respective scale, ...

No planet will look exactly the same. Unless, of course, it is a very simple one. More on that below.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1631005159-472402214.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-1789086190.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-1298994048.jpeg[/img]


[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=4][b]Sub Biomes[/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Caves and underwater sub biomes have also been entirely overhauled.

Tons of new variants have been added underground and just like on the surface, additional objects can spawn to increase variety even more.

﻿[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410276-924973523.jpeg[/img]﻿

Underwater has been completely revamped and is now generated through a triple layered dynamic framework combining assets to generate highly varied and detailed environments.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738939-165524032.jpeg[/img]
[b][size=4]
Unique planets

[/size][/b][size=4][size=3]On top of all the added variety, BPG also uses a flexible dynamic generation framework that can take many shapes[/size][/size] and create countless planetary variations, even when the same environments are being used multiple times.

Each planet generated has its own selection of parts based on its biome. Some liberties have been taken when designing and attributing those parts to the various biomes. Some objects have been injected to improve variety, but some restrictions have also been applied to preserve each biome's identity. Better Planet Generation also introduces countless restored, modified or repurposed assets to the game in order to increase the variety while preserving its visual style.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936068-132859967.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-754906087.jpeg[/img]

[/size][/size][/size][/size]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Natural Generation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is a vastly different experience compared to the unmodded game and even other biome mods.
Not even taking into account the small details, it is more than likely that you will never be able to encounter all the possible assets combinations this mod can generate. Let alone in the different regional layouts each dynamic template can result in.

Each biome has access to multiple procedural templates. Each producing different results in terms of layouts and objects combinations.
Their common goal is to show you a different kind of environment each time. Aesthetically and structurally.
No more "postcard" planets where most of what there is to see is right around the corner. The scale of the generation can get extremely vast compared to the vanilla game.

Planetary generation can now affect your visual enjoyment and the gameplay.
It is a video game, after all.

A world generated at its fullest possible level and highest complexity can take you some time to fully explore on foot. Meaning seeing the most notable regions (and not all of them) and scanning everything.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630052272-1155900954.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-2086924238.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630272224-118529207.jpeg[/img]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]More Variation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

On the other hand, Better Planet Generation also allows more simple, generic yet still visually interesting planets to see :

- Planets only covered in grass and some plants, rocks or both.
- More barren worlds dominated by giant stone or crystal spires.
- Radioactive wastelands.
- Planets dotted with trees or occasional small forests.
- Volcanic wastelands.
- Toxic fields.
- Rocky swamps.
- ...

And the list goes on and on.
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3]The occurence of these "generic" planets only relies on probabilites. None of my templates is designed to specifically produce them.
I made sure they still looked good, though.[/size][/size][/size][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410296-1590906166.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1626079315-1486130072.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Different Experience[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is not for everyone. Planets can be both very detailed in every aspect or very simple.
If you expect to always see trees and a full grass coverage on your Lush planet or anywhere else, there are other mods for that.
This is not what you should expect using BPG.

Now, whether you are a new player ready to explore an infinite universe or a more weathered one that wants to be surprised by the game again, I suggest you give Better Planet Generation a try. It won't harm your game in any way.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629923717-282604290.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410307-2137550589.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=5]WARNING BEFORE INSTALLING :[/size][/b]

Installing this mod will operate changes to the terrain in every biomes.
It is also recommended to install it while in a space station / anomaly / freighter and not on a planet's surface.
Some major updates to the mod can reset the terrain or biome lists.
I'll include a warning on the download page and the sticky when it's the case.[/size][/size][/size][/size]


Recommended :
[/size][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/968]DUD's Sky - Colors[/url] : load planetary colour palettes before BPG to avoid procedural textures conflicts.
[/size][/size]

name: AMUMSS (auto modbuilder-updater with MOD script definition system)
summary: Revolutionary No Man's Sky AMUMSS (auto modbuilder/updater with MOD script definition system)Fully automatic mod builder that automates every step of nms modding and provides an easy to use lua script mod definition system.
author: Mjjstral aka MetaIdea and Wbertro aka TheBossBoy
description:
[color=#ff0000][size=6]-> [/size][size=5]Looking for lua scripts, see:[/size][size=6] [url=https://github.com/MetaIdea/nms-amumss-lua-mod-script-collection]AMUMSS LUA MOD SCRIPT ARCHIVE[/url] <-[/size][/color]

[font=Verdana][color=#ffe599][size=6]AMUMSS is NOT a mod manager, nor can it be used as such.  It is a script processor.[/size][/color][/font]

[color=#ff0000][size=5]AMUMSS does NOT need updating to continue working when NMS updates.[/size]
[size=4]       When the tool MBINCompiler.exe is updated, AMUMSS will download it automatically.[/size][/color]
AMUMSS will auto-update itself (when allowed), if a new version is available (Just execute BUILDMOD.bat as usual and read simple instructions)
[list]
[*]The tools MBINCompiler/libMBIN are auto-updated by AMUMSS.[/*]
[*]Scripts are NEVER updated by AMUMSS, you are responsible for using updated scripts, when they need to be.[/*]
[/list]
[b][b][color=#ff7700][size=3]Questions will be answered if asked in NMS Discord[/size]: here[/color] [url=https://discord.gg/22ZAU9H][color=#00ff00]https://discord.gg/22ZAU9H[/color]
[/url][/b]
IMPORTANT NOTES:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]This tool works as long as MBINCompiler can compile/decompile the MBIN touched by the scripts[/b][/*]
[*][b]NEW version [color=#ff00ff]does[/color] requires [i][color=#ffff00].NET 8 Desktop Runtime x64[/color][/i] to be installed (a MBINCompiler.exe requirement)  It will attempt to auto-install.[/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#ff0000]Note:[/color] Sometimes, your anti-virus may detect some component of AMUMSS and block/quarantine it.  Be assure it is not a virus but its [i][color=#ff0000]behavior [/color][/i]may be interpreted as such by some anti-virus.  Please make sure to create an exception in your anti-virus when this happens.  Also a reboot may be required as some anti-virus do not correctly register the exception when created.[/b][/*]
[/list]
[b][i][size=3]INCLUDES:[/size][/i][/b]
[list]
[*][b][i][size=3][b][i][size=3]NMSPE [/size][/i][/b]([u][b]NMS PCBANKS Explorer)[/b][/u] a [color=#ff0000][b]GUI app to explore libMBIN.dll, NMS PAKS and Unpack/Decompile/Import-Search MXML content[/b][/color][/size][/i][/b][/*]
[*][b][i][size=3][b][i][size=3]AMM [/size][/i][/b]([u][b]_ModScript_Manager)[/b][/u] a [color=#ff0000][b]GUI app simplifying usage of scripts in ModScript folder[/b][/color][/size][/i][/b][/*]
[*][b][i][size=3][b][i][size=3]MFM [/size][/i][/b]([u][b]_MapFileMaker)[/b][/u]: a [color=#ff0000][b]NEW console app to create MapFileTree files from MXMLs using drag/drop[/b][/color][/size][/i][/b][/*]
[/list][b]
[b][color=#ff0000][size=4]Installation: [/size][/color][/b][/b]
[list]
[*][b][size=3][color=#00ff00]See [/color][color=#00ff00][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626][/url][/color][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626[/url]﻿ [color=#00ff00]for detailed instructions![/color][/size][/b]
[b]* [color=#ffff00]Get the latest release from[/color] [url=https://github.com/HolterPhylo/AMUMSS/releases]AMUMSS latest releases on Github Link
[/url]* De-compress the zip file to its own folder (like C:\AMUMSS)   Making the path to AMUMSS main folder short helps prevent bumping against windows path length limit (in rare cases)
* No accented or special characters in the path
* Always extract to a new folder on any drive, never in any System, Documents or game folder
* Create an exception to AMUMSS main folder BEFORE executing anything
[/b][color=#ffff00][b]* If the cmd windows closes immediately (or is blank) when double-clicking BUILDMOD.BAT:
          if you are on windows 7.  Try making '-UseColors N' in BUILDMOD_AUTO.bat and use it instead of BUILDMOD.bat

[/b][/color][/*]

name: Fast Actions 7.1
summary: Faster clicks and key pressed actions
author: Lo2k
description:
Instead of pressing a key for almost one second, this mod provides quicker or instant inputs for :
- menu selection
- creating/dismantling technology
- transfering resources to/from ship
- entering ship
- discussing with NPC
- gathering small plants
- launching refinery processing
- recovering deployable technologies

Enjoy !
[url=http://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/28/?]
[/url]This mod exists in 2 versions :
﻿- instant actions : almost no delay actions (Fractal 4.13 added an in-game option but it only works for a limited range of actions)
- fast actions : between original and instant actions

[color=#ffd966]New : v7.1 fixes precise item quantity amount selection with Instant Actions. (Fast Action is untouched)[/color]

description:
Made it so that everything has the vintage filter, works with Beyond.

The following files get modified by these mods:-
METADATA.EFFECTS.SCREENFILTERS.MBIN
Any other mods that modify the same file will not be compatible.

Installation:
Delete the Disablemods.txt in your PCBANKS folder.
Put ONLY ONE of the mod files in your PCBANKS/MODS folder.

name: Exosolar's and Babs' Beyond Base Building
summary: ★ FULLY MP compatible, this mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options
author: Exosolar Sparky NeptuneX3 Babscoole
description:
[b][color=#f1c232][size=4]What is this Mod?[/size][/color][/b]
[size=4]There are now almost 1,000 buildable base parts in vanilla No Man's Sky! It's a dream come true!
This mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options.
This does NOT mean the mod gives you access to all buildable parts.  You still need to learn the blueprints for each.  :)
Beyond Base Building does NOT add any new build parts to the game.

Now includes all the functionality of gBase Items, [color=#ff0000]if chosen by running the Lua script[/color]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Can multiply power, extraction, and storage rates by 2, 5, or 10. WARNING: Bases built with this mod cannot be uploaded for multiplayer when using 2x, 5x, or 10x multiplied rates.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*][size=4]EM Generators do not need a hotspot and produce 250 power.  Not enabled by default.  Must run Lua through ANUMSS and answer question "Choose a multiplier for Storage and Rates and EMAnywhere status" to generate custom mod file to enable.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]

It is [b]fully compatible[/b] with multiplayer, co-op building, uploading, etc, because it [i]does not add[/i] any parts, which would cause issues in multiplayer.[/size]

[size=4][color=#f1c232][b]★ Beyond Basebuilding[/b] is fully Lua scripted, with script provided for easy updating and merging [b]★[/b][/color] and carries over all of the official updates and improvements offered by Hello Games [b]plus[/b]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Most parts can be Scaled [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] prefab building parts, [color=#fff2cc]Exocraft Geobays, Mineral/Gas Extractors and Base Computer[/color] (Door attachment points bug out when scaled, and issues persist with scaled base computers and geobays).  There may be others not listed.  Be aware, scaling breaks snapping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built in a Freighter.  [color=#fff2cc][i]Exceptions[/i][/color]  include the Base Computer, Industrial Mining parts, Vehicle Summoners and planet-based teleporter.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built at a Planetary Base [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] the freighter teleporter and the Orbital Exocraft Materialiser[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can be built above and below water[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can change color and material[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts, which can be deleted, can be deleted without also deleting attached objects [color=#fff2cc][i]except[/i][/color] Decals and Posters[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]No build-count limits [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] for parts related to resources harvesting, certain terminals, beacons and message capsules (and others with limits that are hard coded into the game, as they are added or changed by Hello Games).[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unlimited Storage Containers[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*This does not increase actual storage amounts: Each numbered container acts as an index to the store rather than a physical box[/i][/size][/color][/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Foundation, Pavings and Communications Station can be placed anywhere (not only on bare terrain)[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Non corvette parts buildable with corvettes[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]
Some customization of the mod is available just by running it through AMUMSS, where you'll be prompted about enabling several feature.  Even more customization can be had by editing the top portion of the Lua before processing.  See Lua usage below for link to AMUMSS install and basic usage How to.[/size]

[color=#f1c232][b][u][size=5]Disclaimer:[/size][/u][/b][/color]
[size=3]This MOD makes changes to the placement and usage setting of vanilla parts.  If the MOD is removed, the vanilla settings will be restored and parts that "violate" a vanilla setting as well as those connected may go "poof".  Best practice is to regularly backup your saves for semi-painless recovery from the unexpected.[/size]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][b][u][color=#f1c232]Installation[/color]
[/u][/b][/size]
[b]Extract archive contents to GAMEDATA\MODS

[color=#f1c232][size=4][u]Lua usage[/u][/size][/color]
[size=4][b]✦[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]How to use AMUMSS at No Man's Sky Nexus - Mods and Community (nexusmods.com)[/url]✦[/b][/size][/b]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]Modified Files[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[color=#d8d8d8][size=3]METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\BASEBUILDINGOBJECTSTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color]

[i][color=#cccccc][size=3]Also check out...[/size][/color][/i]
[size=5]✦[b][color=#ffdd00][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/58018181?tab=user+files]Exosolar's Other Mods[/url][/color][/b]✦[/size]


[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][u][b][color=#f1c232]Is this Mod up-to-date?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4][i][b]Any mod files which are not hidden or demoted to the "Old Files" area can be expected to work.[/b][/i]
All uploaded files (on the Files page) are maintained with their packing date and version of the MBINCompiler used to pack it. Older mod versions, no longer compatible with the current version of No Man's Sky will be demoted to the "Old Files" subsection, but will remain available for download. There are no side-effects to using this mod.[/size]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]How to update, tweak, combine, or patch the mod with AMUMSS?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4]As this mod is now Lua scripted, you can [color=#fff2cc]easily [b]update[/b], [b]tweak[/b] or [b]merge[/b] the mod yourself[/color] (if a game update breaks this PAK of the mod, or you have other PAK or Lua mods that could conflict with this one). [color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*Click on the spoiler below for more[/i][/size][/color][/size]
[spoiler]
[size=3][u]Notes on AMUMSS:[/u]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] tries to update [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases]MBINcompiler[/url] automatically. If it fails to convert EXML/MBIN files, its likely due to a very recent NMS version update and MBINcompiler is awaiting an update too.
If so, I highly recommend you to disable your mods and wait for MBINCompiler to be updated (it's pretty quick in general).[/size]


[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Updating the mod after a game update:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][list]
[*] [size=3]Download [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url], and extract it locally,  avoid placing the AMUMSS folder in a path with special characters or in a system folder like [color=#fff2cc][i]"C:\Program Files (x86)\(...)"[/i][/color].[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Place the mod Lua script (only the .LUA file, not the .PAK file) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]AMUMSS will normally auto-detect the NMS installation folder, but you can also manually edit the path in the [color=#fff2cc][i]NMS_FOLDER.txt[/i][/color] file.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root of the AMUMSS folder and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]A new modded PAK file will be created, using the last update of the MBIN game files duly amended by the script.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]Most of the time simply recompiling the mod using the Lua script will make it compatible again. Use the latest script to ensure you adopt any mod adjustments to accommodate the latest NMS build.[/size][size=3] There are two main causes of mods not correctly updating with this method:
1) MBINCompiler needs an update to be able to decompile the latest version of the game MBIN files.
2) Structural changes have been made to the MBIN files called by this Lua script. Whilst unlikely, this will require some script rewrite and other mods are likely affected.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Tweaking the mod:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]Use the same process as described in [color=#fff2cc][i]Updating the mod[/i][/color].
Just modify the script as you want before recompiling it. Look at the top of my scripts, you can generally edit modifiers there, or even disable/enable some features very easily.[/size]

[size=3][color=#cccccc][i]*[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/]Notepad++[/url] or [url=https://code.visualstudio.com/download/]VSCode[/url] are generally recommended to read EXML and Lua files, due to large file support and automatic highlighting. The [url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/npp-compare/]Compare plugin[/url] for Notepad++, and Lua is also a must-have to highlight file differences.[/i][/color][/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Combining mods that provide Lua scripts:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You'll want to do this if multiple mods affect the same MBIN file.[/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Place all the scripts in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Follow the step, selecting that you want to combine all the scripts into one PAK file, and the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]AMUMSS will output a PAK file that will contain the modifications of all the scripts.[/size]
[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]*If the scripts modify the exact same values in the MBIN file, the last loaded script will overwrite the preceding script values.[/i][/size][/color][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Patch in the mod to make it compatible with other PAK files:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You will want to do this if another mods isn't Lua scripted, and affects the same MBIN file as the Lua scripted mod.

It will work when :
Case 1) you patch a Lua scripted mod for only one other PAK.
Case 2) you patch a Lua scripted mod for several other PAKs, but only if the other PAKs don't modify the same MBIN files between them.[/size]

[size=3][b]How to create a patched PAK:[/b][/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Copy the script and the other mod(s) PAK(s) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS, and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]The new PAK file will contain all the Lua script modifications, and a compatibility patch for the other mod(s) PAK(s).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Rename it something like [color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz Scripted Mod Name -Patched For- The Other Mod Name.pak"[/i][/color].[/size]
[size=3][color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz"[/i][/color] prefix is to ensure that it'll be loaded after the mod(s) it was patched for (for NMS loading order, underscore [i]"_"[/i] came after every other characters).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Remove the original scripted mod PAK from the [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder, and copy both the new patched one, and the other mod(s) PAK(s), into it.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=3][u]Notes:[/u]
[b]Be sure the mod PAK you want to create a compatibility patch for, is updated for the latest NMS version.[/b]
-> When AMUSS find an MBIN file affected by a script and by a PAK in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder, it will take the MBIN file from the mod PAK over the original one of the game, and will apply to it the modifications listed in the script.
So, if the MBIN file of the mod PAK is not updated, the one in the resulting patched PAK won't be either.[/size][/spoiler]
[/spoiler]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]
[color=#f1c232][u][b][size=5]Philosophy[/size][/b][/u][/color]
[size=4]All the erroneous limitations in building are pretty silly, aren't they? In making this mod, I paid specific attention to making sure I did not make changes that will invalidate the bases built with it from online play. Any base made with Beyond BaseBuilding will be fully viable and visible in online play, even when other players don't have this mod! It does this by only editing placement rules while you are in the building editor and not modifying any of the actual base parts themselves.
We hope you enjoy the mod and naturally, your comments are most welcome. We can also be found on the No Man's Sky Discord or reached directly at: [color=#f1c232]Babscoole #6326 [/color]or [color=#f1c232]Exosolar#5120[/color], or if its about the Lua script: [color=#f1c232]NeptuneX3#8095[/color] [size=3][i][size=4]or [/size][/i][/size][color=#f1c232]s p a r k y#0536[/color][/size]


[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

And, of course, thanks to all of the other modders who make mods too, as we often inspect the work of other modders to learn how things are done: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/12249518]RangerDulann[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/1964784]WoodyMontana[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/42286415]jasondude[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/38106355?tab=user+files]Gumsk[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/45932167?tab=user+files]Mjjstral[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/41291360]moddinaccount[/url], Devilin Pixy, saa044, and others have all helped us learn to mod effectively! Without the above-mentioned, their mods and applications, we would be unable to make any mods at all![/i][/size]

3.99: Lots of Endurance "fixes".  GeoBays buildable on Freighters again (Change GEOBAYS_ON_FREIGHTER to true in LUA and run through AMUMSS, false by default).  Added back many other items by default as well.  Farm plants plantable in any biome.

Turn ON and OFF your backpack visibility with a new button in the quick action gesture menu.

This mod is also part of  [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1810]Meta-Mod[/url]﻿ .

MODELS\COMMON\PLAYER\PLAYERCHARACTER\PLAYERCHARACTER\ENTITIES\PLAYERCHARACTER.ENTITY.MBIN

name: NMSEasyTrader
summary:
Trading is a big part in NMS. But having an overview about the economy of all your discovered systems is nearly impossible. NMS don't give us a detailed list and writing down all the systems on a sheet of paper takes just too much time and is boring.
So here is a solution. My tool allows you to manage a list of systems.
author: Weberling2
description:
[b]IMPORTEND: ITS A TOOL OUTSIDE THE GAME (.EXE). ITS REQUIRED TO HAVE A NEWER VERSION OF THE .NET FRAMEWORK TO RUN[/b]

[b]TODO's[/b]
- language files
- calculator with source and destination
- add column with location information

[u]Functions:
[/u]
[u]1. Savefiles
[/u]- Save: Save the current selected Slot
(Often not necessary, because the program automatically saves for certain actions)
- Create Savefile: Creates a savefile with the name of the textbox next to it
- Delete Savefile: Deletes the current selected/loaded file
- Switch between files via dropbox

The files are saved in the Roaming-Directory under /NMSEasyTrader. If a savefile becomes damaged by something, it can't be loaded anymore, but its saved under /NMSEasyTrader/DamagedFiles. I decided to make .xml files, so you can still read the information from the files with notepad++ or something else to recreate your savefile.

[u]2. System-Management
[/u]- Add as new System: at the top there are several boxes (Faction/Eco/Wealth/S/B/Conflict/Name). After putting in all information you can press this button and voila you added a system. By selecting a system on the list, the information is automatically copied into these boxes (a fast way for systems with similar attributes)
- Delete Selected System: Deletes the current selected system
- Overwrite selected System: Overwrites the selected System with the information on top.
NOTE: By selecting a system the information is copied, so pressing the button by accident don't changes the information.
NOTE: There is no undo button!

[u]3. Sorting the list
[/u]Above the list are four dropboxes with default selection "none". Switching f.e. the faction to Gek will only show systems with the attribute Gek.

[u]4. Custom Information
[/u]Next to the list is a blank area. Select a system and write your information there. THEN SELECT A DIFFERENT SYSTEM TO SAVE. THE SAVE BUTTON WON'T SAVE YOUR INFORMATION. 
(Its still a TODO, because there is a difficult interaction with c# listView) 
Systems with custom information are colored green.

[u]5. Hints
[/u]- Well it's a "foreign" executable. So Windows 10 will ask you if you are shure to open the exe.
- I'm doing stuff in your Roaming-Directory. So if the program close itself at start or just don't start then just look if your firewall is blocking it (shouldn't happen, because the Roaming-Directory is a system folder, but sometimes weird things can happen).

[b]BUGS/WISHES...
[/b]For bugs and wishes or just other comments, don't fear to contact me. ^^

If you like my work, then pls share it.
If you love my work, then press the Donate-Button.
(NOTE: it's not commercial, just for motivation ^^)

name: Better Rewards
summary: Increase the amount of currency you get with faster word learning and increased resource gathering options. Frigate (Freighter) Expeditions are also included!
author: MrTrack
description:
Better Rewards increases the amount of units, nanite clusters and quicksilver you get from completing missions or interacting with objects in the world. Non npc word learning (such as knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also faster.

[color=#bf9000][size=3]IMPORTANT NOTE: Don't use this mod when I haven't updated it to the new game version (especially when it is a new or returning expedition)
[/size][/color][color=#bf9000]if you really want to use it when I haven't updated it yet, make sure you [/color][color=#bf9000]back up your save[/color][color=#bf9000] or build the mod using the lua scripts yourself.[/color]

[b]Currency[/b]

Currency gain is roughly increased by 5 times, so as to make it a viable option besides crafting and selling valuable trading goods. Some unit values were tremendously increased (eg.: from minimum amount of 1000-2000 to 20000-50000) like the terminals in abandoned settlements to make the early game less grindy.

Includes:
[list]
[*]Space station missions and Nexus missions
[*]Interactable objects/devices (abandoned buildings, damaged machinery, waypoints, etc.)
[*]Sentinels
[*]Alien interactions
[/list]
[b]Words[/b]

Learning words from non npc interactions (knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also 3 times faster (3 words learned form a single knowledge stone). You now also learn 5 Atlas words, instead of 1 and also have a chance (15%) to learn them when interacting with non npc learning sources.

[b]Resources

[/b]When gathering with the mining beam you generally get 2 times more resources (but only when the things explode as you mine them). Also includes containers, depots, guild rewards, asteroids and ships that drop resources.

[b]Frigate (Freighter) Expedition Rewards

[/b]After a successful expedition, when collecting your rewards you get 5x more units and nanites, 2x more products like Storage Augmentation and NipNip Buds and 3x more resources like Copper, Emeril and Cadmium.
[b]
Installation

[/b]Make sure you delete or edit DISABLEMODS.TXT in your game library (...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS) before trying to use mods. Extract the zip file to ...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder and you are good to go (Create MODS folder if you don't have one). Alternatively you can just use Vortex to download and install.

This mod modifies the [color=#ff0000][size=3]REWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] and [color=#ff0000][size=3]EXPEDITIONREWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] file and will not work with other mods that use those tables.

[b]Updated to NMS version 6.21 (Build ID: 21918502) on 2026.02.13.[/b]

name: Too Many Items Planet Galactic Trade Network
summary: Adds almost all items (products and substances) to Galactic Trade Network terminals on planets.  Most significantly, this includes player built GTN terminals. You may think this is a little cheaty, but it's not. It's super duper cheaty.  You probably shouldn't install it for that reason.
author: Slaymeister
description:
Adds almost all items (products and substances) to Galactic Trade Network terminals on planets.  Most significantly, this includes player built GTN terminals. You may think this is a little cheaty, but it's not. It's super duper cheaty. You probably shouldn't install it for that reason.

LESS CHEATY ALTERNATE POSTED!  SEE BELOW!

The item list includes upgrade modules (Exosuit, craft, ship) available for base currency and a probably some plot items.

Here's what I took out:
[spoiler]I took out the Atlas seeds for some reason, probably because that quest line is in my current to-dos.  There are a few things that don't work out of the player inventory, like items that increase or decrease your faction standing and items that allow you to buy the three game currencies, that I pulled out.  There are also about 500 useless construction items I yanked, as well. If you want to try your hand at the items that don't work, check out the Broken version in the Miscellaneous files. It's just a raw port of the item codes into the store, working or not. Purchasing non-working items didn't hurt my game, I just ended up deleting things that didn't do anything from inventory.[/spoiler]

I built this mod because I don't have time for or interest in grinding for resources. If you're playing this game for the rush of achievement after hours of incremental improvement, this mod will ruin the game for you.

SLIGHTLY LESS CHEATY VERSION: I have published a slightly less cheaty version that has all craftable items removed. That means if you can make it, you're going to have to. I did make an exception for all items that are normally in the planet shops.  Those items that can possibly be present in the shop without mods will always be present with this mod.  Taking out all craftable or broken items and guaranteeing all vanilla possible items puts 644 items always in the shop. The intention is to not obviate the crafting system in the game.

Here's how I built this mod:
[spoiler]I built this mod by loading the EXML files into a spreadsheet that pulled out the IDs, then built up a store item entry using those IDs. I added an exclude list feature and cleaned it up a bit to make it fairly self explanatory to anyone whose dug into modding NMS even a little. Should someone want to steal this mod or update it after this covid thing has past and companies are hiring again leaving me with (hopefully) little time for games, this spreadsheet would make said larceny a snap. I've uploaded this spreadsheet. By all means, larcen to your heart's content.[/spoiler]

Modifies DEFAULTREALITY.MBIN and will conflict with anything else that also does.

name: NomNom
summary: NomNom is the most complete savegame editor for NMS but also shows you additional information around the data you're about to change. You can also easily look up each item individually to examine its attributes, independently of a savegame, or get other useful information that are not related to a specific one (but enhanced if one is loaded).
author: zencq
description:
[color=#e69138][size=3][b]NomNom is now in beta state.[/b] This means for you that some things may still not be 100% finished but the general state of the tool is a lot better than before.[/size] If you encounter bugs or when you think something doesn't work as expected or could be improved, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1566?tab=bugs]let me know[/url]![/color]

[color=#ff0000]All available features are tested while implemented but mistakes can happen, so be aware of that and backup your saves![/color]

The features can be divided into the different main parts:
[list]
[*][b]Manager[/b] Manage your saves!
[list]
[*]Automatic backup.[/*]
[*]Save your save as human-readable JSON.[/*]
[*]Copy, move, and swap slots to another.[/*]
[*]Delete your save.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]Editor[/b] Edit your save for your needs!
[list]
[*]Ability to manage fleets, change data values like currencies and stats, and organize inventories.[/*]
[*]Ability to fast travel to any system you like, trigger space battles, and clear portal interference.[/*]
[*]Ability to edit your knowledge and recorded experiences.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
Have a look at the screenshots as well, to see what NomNom is capable of.

Each version of NomNom is built with the latest game version (at that time) in mind and the version number is reflecting that. Each one is also backwards
compatible down to [b]Beyond 2.11[/b] and even saves before that can still be edited via the build-in JSON editor. If you use it with a newer game version branch than
the one it was built for (e.g. [b]7.00[/b]), things should work as usual in most cases but there can always be a breaking change.

NomNom is compatible with every platform No Man's Sky is available on (some work better than others though). You can select a specific account/folder with you saves or, for platforms on PC, one level above if you have multiple accounts. A complete and always up-to-date overview with additional notes can be found [url=https://github.com/zencq/libNOM.io?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started]on GitHub[/url].


[b]Instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]After downloading and extracting the zip file you'll find a few files. All you need to care about is the executable ([b]NomNom.exe[/b]) but new folders may    be created at runtime (e.g. for backups) that will become relevant to you.[/*]
[*]You may want to create a shortcut to the executable for easier access.[/*]
[*]As the tool includes an automatic backup functionality you don't need to do it manually but if you want to be absolutely safe, do it.[/*]
[*]At first start the tool locates your saves at the default location of each platform but if that fails, you must select it manually.[/*]
[*]Select a slot.[/*]
[*]Start tinkering![/*]
[/list]

If you like NomNom and want to support me in its further development, you can do so via the donation options above or on [url=https://www.buymeacoffee.com/cengelha]Buy Me a Coffee[/url], [url=https://github.com/sponsors/cengelha]GitHub[/url], [url=https://ko-fi.com/cengelha]Ko-fi[/url], and [url=https://www.patreon.com/cengelha]Patreon[/url]. I will appreciate it!
There won't be a paywall though.

The is also a dedicated [url=https://discord.gg/nomnom-762409407488720918]Discord[/url] server where you'll find all information in one place, firsthand. Please read the rules first, to gain full access. If you need (or want to offer) help, found a bug, have a suggestion, or something else regarding NomNom, you will find, or can post it there.

Issues created here on Nexus Mods or via another channel will of course also be addressed.


Header image by [url=https://patreon.com/Orioto]Orioto[/url]﻿.

name: Harsh Economy
summary: Makes it much harder to make money by drastically increasing buy-prices (but not sell-prices), reducing what you get from cargo drops, increasing some component build-costs, reducing the value of salvage/ancient bones/storm crystals, and many other changes.  Works best with a new game.
author: Tooms79
description:
I felt is was too easy to make units early in a game.  Within a couple of hours of starting a new game you could easily buy an S-Class scanner upgrade, or collect fossils, or storm crystals, etc.  The units would roll in very quickly and... I wanted it to take much longer to even feel like you were slightly established.

Here is a more comprehensive list of the changes and the rationale:[list]
[*]Your starting ship and multi-tool are permanently broken.  Your ship slots may look repairable.  They're not; fixing it just makes it so you can move the broken bit to occupy a technology slot.  This makes it so units are even more desirable at the start of the game.
[*]You can't just fly away other derelict ships.  I've done this by making them need a circuit board to repair (and giving you one at the start so you can fix your starting ship).  I recommend turning breakable-technology off in your difficulty settings lest you accidentally strand yourself somewhere due to this change.
[*]There is now a large price differential between buying and selling.  If you want to make money by trading, this probably isn't the mod for you.
[*]Nav data is cheaper - this was a very easy source of (very) early game income & has therefore been removed.
[*]Salvaged data is cheaper
[*]Ancient bones / salvage / storm crystals are now cheaper
[*]The build cost of antimatter has been drastically increased.  I wanted to feel like having access to a new system was much more of an event, and now it is.  You (mostly) won't be handed antimatter or hyperdrive fuel by anyone either.
[*]Scanner upgrades are now build-able rather than purchase-able (I couldn't see how to actually remove from the shop so instead have just absurdly inflated the price).  You can find the new recipes on the anomaly.  I am not 100% happy with how this works now, but it's functional and I can't see a better way (yet).
[*]As purchase-able upgrades were generally better than the recipes you can unlock, I felt their nanite cost should be higher.  I have slightly increased the nanite rewards you get from some sources to compensate.
[*]The rewards you get from cargo drops, jettison pods, etc. have been lowered.  You also can't get microchips from them, meaning you do actually have to earn units as the tutorial quest tells you to do!
[*]The rewards locked behind having Atlas Pass 1 are unchanged, but the pass is now harder to build.
[/list]
The mod is called Harsh Economy for a reason.  It is meant to be harsh.  It probably isn't for most people.


Replaces these files if you're worried about conflicts with other mods:
\METADATA\GAMESTATE\DEFAULTSAVEDATA.MBIN
\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\NMS_REALITY_GCPRODUCTTABLE.MBIN
\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\NMS_REALITY_GCRECIPETABLE.MBIN
\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\NMS_REALITY_GCSUBSTANCETABLE.MBIN
\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\NMS_REALITY_GCTECHNOLOGYTABLE.MBIN
\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\PROCEDURALPRODUCTTABLE.MBIN
\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\REWARDTABLE.MBIN
\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\UNLOCKABLEITEMTREES.MBIN
\METADATA\SIMULATION\MISSIONS\TUTORIALMISSIONTABLE.MBIN
\MODELS\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\CRATE\UNDERGROUNDCRATE\ENTITIES\UNDERGROUNDCRATE.ENTITY.MBIN

Note the Worlds 2 update changed where you install mods.  They no longer go in the PCBANKS folder.  It's like this instead:
...\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS\Harsh_Economy_Worlds2\...

Delete No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/DISABLEMODS.txt if it exists

This mod is incompatible with any other mod that modifies GCGAMEPLAYGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN

MOD is compatible with Expeditions

Uninstall MOD
Delete the ScanNow.pak or ScanNow_OneSec.pak file from No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/MODS

name: gCreatures Giant Creature Animal Sizes - EXML
summary: Increase maximum possible creature sizes.
author: Gumsk
description:
[size=2]✅ Compatible - EXML patch mod - likely to work well with all other mods
✅ Update Safe - Likely to survive updates[/size]



[size=4]This mod increases the maximum size of all creatures, making most of them bigger.
[/size][list]
[*][size=4]1.4x: Not a significant increase. You may not even consciously notice it.[/size]
[*][size=4]2x: A noticeable increase, but still not crazy.[/size]

[/list][size=4]
Some notes and caveats:
[/size][list]
[*][size=4]This will also decrease how many small creatures there are, though they can still be just as small as before.[/size]

[/list]

name: gShip - Gumsk's Custom Ships
summary: Adds over 70 new ships. Does not replace any ships and won't crash multiplayer. Added two color variations of Firefly's Serenity and a resize of X70B Phantom. More ships coming soon.
author: Gumsk
description:
[u][b][size=3]Updates[/size][/b][/u]
[list]
[*]All existing individual model versions have been incorporated into the main PAK
[*]Seed list has been updated. I can't seem to find the purple Jedi interceptor, so if you find the seed, please let me know.
[*]Now that I'm on a good PC with 4k resolution, I can tell that some of the textures are absolutely awful. I will start updating those soon.
[/list]

[b][u][size=3]Description[/size][/u][/b]
This mod is a descendant of [url=http://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1064]WinderTP's Ships of Moar[/url] and uses much of that knowledge to add many (currently 70) new ships to the game.
[list]
[*]These ships do not replace any existing models, so your old ships are safe.
[*]You will not see these ships in the wild on NPCs.
[*]These custom ships won't break multiplayer. Other players still won't see your custom ship; they'll just see a Golden Vector.
[*]A ship summoner is included in optional files so you don't have to save edit or do anything else to get them. It is based almost entirely on Mjjstral's emote summoning work, so thanks to them. There are S-Class and a C-Class summoners for whatever power level you want. I highly recommend you use the save editor method, though.
[*]When there are new ships added, the seed values might change on your ship. Just use the save editor to update the seed value, or use the summoner again to get a new ship.
[*]The S-class ship summoner includes the advanced ship tech from Expedition 3.
[/list]
The mod works by making the Golden Vector scene procedural, then adding new ships to that procedural list. I will always make it so that seed 0x1 is the original Golden Vector, so a default Golden Vector will stay as such.


[b][u][size=3]How to Use - Option One (Recommended)[/size][/u][/b]
(Scroll all the way down for detailed instructions with pictures) Install the main Custom Ships mod (the really big file). Name the ships you want to change to something obvious, like TIE Silencer and save the game. Open NMS Save Editor by Goatfungus (you can get it [url=https://github.com/goatfungus/NMSSaveEditor]here[/url]). Go to the ships tab and find the ship you renamed. Make sure the Type is set to "Golden Vector". Set the Seed value to the appropriate value below. Save your changes and load your game.

[b][u][size=3]How to Use - Option Two (Not Recommended)[/size][/u][/b]
This method is not recommended, as there are some bugs with the summoner mod and the save editor method is easy to use now. If you want to do it though:
Install both the Custom Ship mod and the Custom Ship Summoner mod from optional files. When you load the game, use the appropriate emote to summon the ship you want and swap it with your current ship. The ship will initially appear bright silver, without textures. Once you have traded the ship, saved, and reloaded, the textures will appear normally. If you get an empty exchange screen, cancel it; don't accept an empty trade as it can mess up your save file. Once you have summoned all the ships you want, you can uninstall the Custom Ship Summoner. If your character just raises their arms and nothing else happens (T-pose), you likely have a mod conflict with some other mod that alters the rewards table.


For many of these, I highly recommend my [url=http://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1723]GShip Trails[/url] mod to hide the trails or make them match the colors of the ship. If you have feedback or suggestions, please let me know in the comments. Special thanks to WinderTP, Kibbles, MonkeyMan192, and Mjjstral for their expertise, help, and patience, and to the model creators on Sketchfab. This is mostly a derivation of the Ships of Moar mod, which you should also look at.[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1541/]


[/url][b][u]Detailed Instructions with Pictures

[/u][/b]1. Make sure you downloaded the latest PAK file from this mod page and put it in your PCBANKS\MODS folder.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/ChDc4xJ/MODS-Folder.png[/img]﻿

2. Make sure you removed DISABLEMODS.TXT from your PCBANKS folder.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/m8ny61x/PCBANKS.png[/img]

3. Make sure you selected the proper save game file in your save editor. Note that for each save there are two files, one for autosave and one for "restore points" or manual saves; I believe odd numbers are auto and even numbers are manual. This is important for knowing which game to load later. In this example, we are using the auto-save. Note that if you are editing the auto-save, the game can overwrite your changes between when you change them in the save editor, save in save editor, and load the save in game. You need to be fast and double/triple-check that your changes have actually been made.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/vzW11vR/Save-Editor-Save-Selection.png[/img]﻿

4. Lookup the seed value you want on this page. For this example, we are using X-Wing White.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/D8T2vJK/X-Wing-White-Seed.png[/img]

5. Go to the Ships tab and change the name and class to whatever you want, the type to Golden Vector, and the seed to which ship you want.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/2Pv6MKk/X-Wing-White-Save-Editor.png[/img]

6. Remember to go back to the main tab of the save editor and Save Changes.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/dfgMPh4/Save-Editor-Save-Changes.png[/img]

7. Load your NMS game. If the ship doesn't appear properly, make sure you chose the correct save file to load. In this example, we are using the auto-save.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/whtmthQ/Autosave.png[/img]

8. You should see your new ship in game.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/rbtN18j/X-Wing-White-In-Game.png[/img]

name: Inertia Drifto - Exocraft Speed and Boost Enhancer
summary: Boosting exocraft speeds and boost capabilities, making them actually fast
author: WinderTP
description:
[center][/center][center][size=4][u]Déjà vu...
You have been to this page before[/u][/size][/center]
[center][youtube]oBmGhQnS6RE[/youtube][/center]
[center]﻿[/center][center][b][size=4]Inertia Drifto was originally made as an attempt to make the roamer driftable without upgrades, whether it succeeds is not important.
Also exocraft boosting go bbbrrrrr 
[/size][/b]
[size=5][b]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1948/]AE86 replacer for Roamer[/url]﻿ for the best immersion[/b][/size][/center]

[u][size=5][b]Inertia Drifto boosts exocraft performance, including:[/b][/size][/u]
[list]
[*]Increases Top Speed of all exocrafts between 208.333333333% - 312.5%
[*]Increases Top Boosting Speed of all exocrafts between 50% - 200%
[*]Increases Acceleration of all exocrafts between 127.2727272727% - 150%
[*]Increases Boosting capacity by 66.6666666% - 900%
[*]Decreases Boosting charge time by 81.8181818181% - 300%
[*]Increases Mining Laser mining speed by 300%
[*]Increases Mining Laser mining damage by 500%
[*]Decreases exocraft Mining Laser energy drain rate by 83.33333333333333%
[*]Increases exocraft base summoning range to 10000u (or by 900% on land and 2400% underwater, depending on which variable the game uses, I don't really know)
[*]Decreases Fuel drain rate by 62.5%
[*]Decreases Boosting Fuel drain rate by 90% (75% in survival)
[/list]Custom exocraft models from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1067]Car Boys[/url].
[center][url=https://nomanssky.fandom.com/wiki/Mods#Installing_Mods][size=6]Installing Mods Manually[/size][/url][/center][size=6][center][url=https://stepmodifications.org/wiki/NoMansSky:Tutorials/HowToAMUMSS]How To merge with AMUMSS[/url]
[url=https://stepmodifications.org/wiki/NoMansSky:Tutorials/Merging_two_mods]How to merge without AMUMSS[/url]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]How to use AMUMSS (pdf)[/url][/center][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957][size=5][b][center]Click here to go to AMUMSS's Nexus mod page.[/center][/b][/size][/url]
[u][size=4][b]ALL EXML files are configured to be maximally compatible with other mods and require no merging via AMUMSS[/b][/size][/u]
EDITS GLOBALS\GCVEHICLEGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML

This mod is provided as-is, thus will only be updated as long as I use it.
AMUMSS script is provided, however, and everyone is welcome to create their own versions with it.

name: Rohtang's Cinematography BuildCam Rework (WIP)
summary:
Firstly ---THIS IS A WIP MOD---

This mod was born from countless hours of searching the internet for a mod that unfreezes time in photo mode for single player.
After hours of searching for myself I decided to modify the build camera.
This mod makes cinematography fun, giving you a camera like photo mode without time freeze.
author: Rohtang13
description:
[font=Tahoma][size=4][i][b]IMPORTANT: [/b][/i][/size][/font][font=Tahoma]
-This is a WIP and it's a bit of a [s]hack job[/s].
-Some icons are missing from the [b]QUICK/BUILD MENUS[/b] but the text is still there so you can still use it somewhat effectively. (This is not a bug. Due to my lack of knowledge on modding this is the best I can do at the moment)

[font=Tahoma][size=4][size=3][b][font=Tahoma][size=4][size=4][font=Tahoma]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/font][/size][/size][/font][/b][/size][/size][/font]

[size=4][i][b]FEATURES:[/b][/i][/size]
[size=3]-[i]Extended[/i] the BuildCam to [b]650[/b]
-[i]Removed[/i] [b]Clipping[/b] from BuildCam
-[i]Removed[/i] some UI from BuildCam to create a makeshift [b]"VideoMode"[/b]
-[i]Added[/i] 360 Ship View
[/size]
[size=4][size=3][b][font=Tahoma][size=4][size=4][font=Tahoma]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/font][/size][/size][/font][/b][/size][/size]
[u][b]
How To Use:

[/b][/u][b]Step 1[/b] - Disable HUD
[b]Step 2[/b] - Enter BuildCam
[b]Step 3[/b] - Hold the Sub Menu Button (on PC it's [i][b]left ctrl[/b][/i])
[b]Step 4[/b] - Record Your Scene!
[/font][size=4][size=3][b][font=Tahoma][size=4]
[size=4][font=Tahoma]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This mod changes[b]- [i]GCCAMERAGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN [/i][/b][i]&[b] HUDBUILD.MBIN[/b][/i][/font][/size][u]
[/u][/size][/font][/b][b][font=Tahoma][size=4][u][size=4][size=3]
[i]Using a controller is recommended for smoother shots but not required[/i].

[/size][/size][/u][size=2]Disclaimer:[/size][/size][/font][/b][font=Tahoma][size=2] [i]I've done as much as I can with my knowledge of modding No Man's Sky at this time. I will continue to update this for future patches until Hello Games adds a better feature (hopefully). If anybody with the knowledge to improve on this mod and would like to, can do so. [/i][/size][/font][b][font=Tahoma][size=4][u]
[/u][/size][/font][/b][/size][/size][size=3]
[/size]

name: No Small Freighters
summary: Removes the small cargo pod ships and frigates from the NPC fleets. Also has an option to only remove cargo pods, keeping frigates for recruiting.
author: Lenni
description:
Removed the small cargo pod ships and frigates from the NPC fleets. Useful for taking screenshots without having shadows or for attacking freighters without having to worry about standing.

Modified file:
AISPACESHIPMANAGER.MBIN

✅ Patch mod - likely to work well with other Patch and Overwrite mods

name: BuildFrame WENIS - Wall Elements eNforced Intact-keeping or Substitution
summary: Allows customisation of contextual base walls behaviour via AMUMSS script
author: WinderTP
description:
[center][font=Lucida Sans Unicode][size=6]This mod has been made obsolete by [url=https://www.nomanssky.com/endurance-update/]NMS update 3.94[/url]﻿
[img]https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/215514674869829633/999300929373351937/unknown.png[/img]﻿

WENIS[/size]
[size=5][u](Wall Elements eNforced Intact-keeping or Substitution)[/u]

[b]is a part of[/b]
[u][img]https://i.imgur.com/gy8ND8k.png[/img][/u][b][font=Lucida Sans Unicode][size=4]A framework focused on integrating various basebuilding mods into one playable and accessible environment.
[/size][/font][/b][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2197][/url][/size][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2197]RecTUM - Recategorisation and Trimming Utility for Build Menu[/url]﻿
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2215]SACS - Selection Augmentation for Colour System
[/url][/size][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2281][s]WENIS - Wall Elements eNforced Intact-keeping or Substitution
[/s][/url][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2604]MILF - Build Menu Infrastructure Listings from Foundation[/url][/size][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2281][/url]﻿
[/size][/size][/font][/center]


[u][b][size=6]Why make WENIS?[/size][/b][/u]
[size=3]
[center][/center]The idea came with several discord messages and Reddit comments. In the Frontier update, along with new base objects, a new mechanic was implemented: 

[quote]Structural base parts such as walls, windows and arches will now intelligently select an appropriate variation – foundation, mid or top – for their position within a structure, making it quick and easy to construct aesthetically pleasing and highly varied bases.[/quote]
The comments we received mainly focused on the inability to [u][b]disable them[/b][/u], but they did not specify which part ("[i]foundation, mid or top[/i]", as the quote described) a mod should default to. As a result, rather than making a script that would change the parts into a fixed model, we have developed WENIS with [b]full customisation[/b] in mind.

WENIS is designed to be easy to use for beginners, with advanced users able to fully customise each object by their relative wall position. It is achieved by [b][u]replacing the model paths of the variations (top, middle, or bottom) with paths of another contextual variation[/u][/b]. As a result, all walls can be changed to look like another variation.

[center]﻿[img]https://media1.tenor.com/images/9f85b9ed42397516b5b8a27a7508bd8a/tenor.gif[/img]﻿[/center]

WENIS provides [b][u]10 presets[/u][/b] which the user can choose with the [i]PRESET[/i] parameter to easily swap parts. Examples of each preset with a "Wall" object in all three contextual positions (top, middle, bottom) are available to view in the [b]IMAGES[/b] section.

[/size][center][img]https://media1.tenor.com/images/4602137b95fe90499915bdc800b50436/tenor.gif?itemid=25648143[/img]﻿﻿[/center]

[size=3]If the user desires to [b][u]fully customise[/u][/b] each wall object's contextual variation, they can navigate to the [i]CHANGE_CHOICE[/i] table to [b]change an object's contextual variation, by material, by position[/b].

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/OuatXOI.png[/img]﻿[/center][/size]

[size=3]Below is the list of objects corresponding to the names of entries under [/size][size=3][i]CHANGE_CHOICE[/i], each object can be [b]individually customised by each contextual variation (top, middle, bottom)[/b], to use the options specified within [i]CHANGE_CHOICE[/i], leave the [i]PRESET[/i] parameter blank. Read instructions inside the .lua script for a more comprehensive information:[/size]
 
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/egfqBe5.jpg[/img]﻿﻿[/center]




[b][u][size=6]Installation[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]WENIS can be used standalone, although it is designed to be used with other BuildFrame modules and modded objects.

Because of this, [b][u]WENIS is designed to be used as an AMUMSS .lua script[/u][/b], to be used along with any .paks or .luas that other basebuilding mods provide.[/size]

[quote][size=6]Important: T[/size][size=5]o use the options specified within [i]CHANGE_CHOICE[/i], leave the [i]PRESET[/i] parameter blank.[/size][/quote]

[size=4]Below is the "How to use" section from the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS page[/url] for luas alone:[/size]

[list]
[/list][list=1]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS]Unzip download into a folder like C:\AMUMSS (not under any OS controlled folder)[/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS]Choose/Copy a script from the ModScriptCollection folder or from anywhere else or create one yourself[/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS]Paste it into the ModScript folder[/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS]Start (double-click) BuildMod.bat[/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS]If asked, put your No Man's Sky game folder path into NMS_FOLDER.txt, otherwise the tool will find the game files[/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS]Answer a few questions and the tool will do its processing, let it finish (review the REPORT.txt file if necessary)[/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS]Copy the mod that gets created in the CreatedModPAKs folder to your game folder if you haven't made that choice at the start of processing Note: You can combine multiple mods and even make PATCH mods[/font]
[/list]

[size=4]And below are the instructions for using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] with both luas and [u][b]one[/b][/u] pak, from "Creating a Patch for existing MOD PAKs":[/size]

[list=1]
[*][size=3]Copy the script AND the MOD PAKs you want to patch to the ModScript folder [/size][font=Arial][size=2](WARNING: Having more than one pak in ModScript will NOT combine both paks if they modify the same file, only the last one loaded will combine with the script(s), AMUMSS can handle correctly multiple paks in ModScript but be aware that only the last mbin file loaded will be the one used by the script(s))[/size][/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]MODBUILDER will attempt to use your MBIN_FILE_SOURCE named in the script by searching for it in the mod PAK(s)[/size][/font] [font=Arial][size=2] (If found, that will preserve the mod PAK changes UNLESS you have changed the exact same values with your script)[/size][/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]A new mod PAK will be created in the CreatedModPAKs folder[/size][/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]Place BOTH files (all original PAKs and PATCH pak) into your NMS MODS folder if you did not let MODBUILDER copy it to MODS for you[/size][/font]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]Verify that the DISABLEMODS.TXT file in PCBANKS folder is still deleted if you did not let MODBUILDER delete it for you[/size][/font]
[/list]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957][size=5][b]Click here to go to AMUMSS's Nexus mod page.[/b][/size][/url]

[size=4]When used alone, the output .pak name will be [b][u]"~~~WENIS.pak"[/u][/b]; when used in conjunction with other luas, the .pak name will be [b][u]"~~~~BuildFrame_Comp.pak"[/u][/b] (or whatever the last lua that dictates the MOD_BATCHNAME to be)[/size]


[b][u][size=6]Compatibility[/size][/u][/b]
[size=3]
WENIS is designed to be [b][u]processed first in AMUMSS[/u][/b], before most other scripts. This effectively only allows AMUMSS to search through vanilla entries (which WENIS edits only and not modded ones), and shorten processing time as a result.

As a side-effect, any other lua that modifies the same entries -[code](WALL, WALL_H, WALLDIAGONAL, WALL_WINDOW0, WALL_WINDOW1, WALL_WINDOW2, WALL_WINDOW3, WALL_DOOR0, WALL_DOOR1, WALL_DOOR0_H, WALL_DOORWINDOW0, WALL_DOORGARAGE0, WALL_ARCH, WALL_ARCH_H, list not fully descriptive, only use as approximiation of true IDs)[/code]will overwrite WENIS's changes, although this would be unlikely as there is no other mod that achieve the same result as WENIS.

[b]For more information, feel free to join the [url=https://discord.gg/kFxjuuj]modding discord[/url] and discuss with us further.[/b]

Edits
METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\BASEBUILDINGPARTSTABLE.MBIN

name: Quick Breeder
summary: This mod drastically shortens the timers for each step of the creature breeding process. (3 options)
author: Mantidae
description:
A simple tweak to the Companions system that makes breeding new pets much more practical and less time consuming. No more waiting 3+ days to add another ugly lil' gremlin baby to your collection.

This mod changes the values of PetGrowthTime, PetIncubationTime, PetEggLayingInterval, PetEggFirstDelay, and PetEggModificationTime from the Creatures global file. The new timer values of each version and a comparison to the vanilla timers can be found in the images.

name: Planetary System Scanner - Rework by Azunain
summary: Reworks the Save Point into a planetary scanner, letting you scan all planetary resources in a system without flying to each planet. Includes multiple variants with different Navigation Data costs and full multi-language support.
author: azunain
description:
[center][size=6][b]Planetary System Scanner - Rework by Azunain[/b][/size]
[i]Tested for: No Man’s Sky 6.0.3 (Public)[/i][/center]

This is a modernized rework of [i]Planetary System Scanner[/i], originally by [b]Aristotale[/b] (uploaded by [b]decamhian[/b]). It makes the [b]Save Point[/b] act like a [i]Freighter Scanner Room[/i] from the surface: scan a whole system’s planetary resources [b]without flying to each planet[/b]. Each scan consumes [b]Navigation Data[/b] (configurable variants below).

[line]
[size=4]🛠️ What’s new[/size]
[list]
[*]Updated for game version [b]6.0.3[/b].
[*][b]EXML-based release[/b] (no .pak). The original [b].lua[/b] is included for AMUMSS users.
[*]Charges [b]Navigation Data[/b] on every scan (no free repeats).
[*]Full multi-language localisation via a standalone [b]LocTable.MXML[/b] shipped at the [b]mod root[/b] (no edits to LOC1 MBINs).
[*]Clean file footprint: [b]edits the Save Point .ENTITY[/b] and [b]adds LocTable.MXML[/b].
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🔧 How it works — step by step[/size]
[b]TL;DR:[/b] Unlock the [b]Save Point[/b] blueprint at the Anomaly, build it at your base, interact to scan the current system. Each scan costs [b]Navigation Data[/b].

[b]1) Unlock the blueprint (first time only)[/b]
[list]
[*]Go to the [b]Anomaly[/b] → talk to the [b]Construction Research Unit[/b] (base building research).
[*]In many saves the Save Point sits behind this path in the tree:
[i]Save Beacon → Base Teleport Module → Galactic Trade Terminal → Save Point[/i]. With this mod, the Save Point is [b]renamed[/b] in the UI to [b]“Planetary System Scanner”[/b], so that’s what you’ll see once it’s reachable.[*]Spend [b]Salvaged Data[/b] to unlock it. If you’ve already unlocked the Save Point in your save, you can skip this.
[/list]

[b]2) Build it at your base[/b]
[list]
[*]Open the build menu ([i]Z[/i] on PC) and place the [b]Save Point[/b] ([i]may appear as “Planetary System Scanner”[/i]) inside your base build area.
[*]Icon/model is the standard Save Point; only the [b]name[/b] and [b]behavior[/b] are changed by the mod.
[/list]

[b]3) Use it to scan a system[/b]
[list]
[*]Interact with the device (default [i]E[/i]) → it performs a [b]system-wide planetary resource scan[/b] (like the freighter Scanner Room).
[*]Each use consumes [b]Navigation Data[/b] according to the variant you installed ([i]x1, x2, x3, x5, x10[/i]).
[*]Results: planet resources for every body in the current system are revealed. Check via your [b]Discoveries[/b] or by examining planets/planetside HUD.
[*]Scan again when you move to a [b]new star system[/b].
[/list]

[b]4) Where to get Navigation Data[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Orange data boxes[/b] on tables in buildings/space stations.
[*]Trade with the [b]Cartographer[/b] on space stations (Nav Data ↔ charts).
[*]Occasional containers, observatories, and minor settlements.
[/list]

[i]Notes:[/i]
[list]
[*][b]Save Beacon vs Save Point:[/b] The device this mod changes is the [b]Save Point[/b] (small tripod-like pad). “Save Beacon” is a different item in the tree; you may need to unlock it en route to the Save Point depending on tree layout.
[*]No freighter required. Works on any planet where you can build a base.
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🔥 Choose your Navigation Data cost[/size]
Pick one variant (each charges per scan):
[list]
[*]🟢 [b]x1[/b] — Minimal cost
[*]🟢 [b]x2[/b] — Slightly higher
[*]🟡 [b]x3[/b] — Balanced
[*]🟠 [b]x5[/b] — Discourages spam
[*]🔴 [b]x10[/b] — Hardcore economy
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🗂️ Files (EXML override)[/size]
[b]Edited[/b]
[code]
MODELS/PLANETS/BIOMES/COMMON/BUILDINGS/PARTS/BUILDABLEPARTS/TECH/SAVEPOINT/ENTITIES/SAVEPOINT.ENTITY.MBIN
[/code]
[b]Added[/b]
[code]
LocTable.MXML (placed at the root of the mod folder)
[/code]
[i]Note:[/i] Localisation is provided by the standalone [b]LocTable.MXML[/b] at the mod root. This mod does not edit any [b]LANGUAGE/NMS_LOC1_*.MBIN[/b] files.

[line]
[size=4]🛠️ Installation (manual EXML override)[/size]
[b]This mod ships as loose EXML/MXML files (no .pak).[/b] Install them as an “EXML override” so the game (or your loader) picks them up.

[b]1) Close the game.[/b]

[b]2) Locate your No Man’s Sky installation folder[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Steam (Windows):[/b]
[code]...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\[/code][*][b]GOG (Windows):[/b]
[code]...\GOG Galaxy\Games\No Man's Sky\[/code][*][b]Linux/Steam Deck (Proton):[/b]
[code]~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/No Man's Sky/[/code][*][b]macOS (App bundle):[/b]
Right-click the app → [i]Show Package Contents[/i] → [code]/Applications/No Man's Sky.app/Contents/Resources/No Man's Sky/[/code][/list]

[b]3) Create an EXML override folder (one-time setup)[/b]
If you already use an EXML/MXML loader, use its root. Otherwise, the simplest convention used by my mods is:
[code]<No Man's Sky>\GAMEDATA\MODS\[/code]
Create it if it doesn’t exist.

[b]4) Copy this mod’s folder into your override root[/b]
The final structure should look like this (example):
[code]
<No Man's Sky>\GAMEDATA\MODS\
└─ HardcoreSky_SavepointAsScanner_NAVx5
├─ LocTable.MXML
└─ MODELS
└─ PLANETS
└─ BIOMES
└─ COMMON
└─ BUILDINGS
└─ PARTS
└─ BUILDABLEPARTS
└─ TECH
└─ SAVEPOINT
└─ ENTITIES
└─ SAVEPOINT.ENTITY.EXML
[/code]
[b]Important:[/b] Keep the internal folders exactly as shown (paths and names matter).

[b]5) (Optional, for .pak users)[/b] If you also use traditional [.pak] mods, make sure vanilla mod blocking is disabled:
Delete or rename:
[code]<No Man's Sky>\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\DISABLEMODS.TXT[/code]
…and place your [.pak] files in:
[code]<No Man's Sky>\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS\[/code]
(Loose EXML/MXML in [i]GAMEDATA\MODS[/i] can coexist with .pak mods.)

[b]6) Launch the game and verify[/b]
[list]
[*]Build a [b]Save Point[/b] at your base, interact with it, and confirm it scans the current star system.
[*]If text shows as IDs (e.g., UI_PLANET_SCANNER_LABEL), ensure [b]LocTable.MXML[/b] is present at the mod folder’s root.
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]⚠️ Compatibility[/size]
[list]
[*]Conflicts with mods that modify the Save Point interaction component in [b]SAVEPOINT.ENTITY.MBIN[/b].
[*]Generally safe with language mods, since localisation is shipped as a separate [b]LocTable.MXML[/b]. Only conflicts if another mod overwrites the same file at the mod root.
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🧪 Tested with[/size]
[list]
[*]Game build: [b]6.0.3 (Public)[/b]
[*]MBINCompiler [b]v6.03.0-pre2[/b] via AMUMSS [b]v5.4.4.5w[/b]
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🧾 Credits[/size]
[list]
[*]Original concept & implementation: [b]Aristotale[/b] (upload by [b]decamhian[/b])
[*]Rework & maintenance: [b]Azunain (HardcoreSky)[/b]
[/list]

Living Ship Launch Systems are more alive than ever, and they're HUNGRY!

- Charge the Neural Assembly (launch thrusters) with larval cores, hypnotic eyes, or all manner of abyssal/stellar dishes. Cooked dishes will be particularly effective.
- Upgrades to Neural Assembly are unchanged, but more impactful due to the altered launch systems, providing more sense of progression.

[size=4]Look, the important thing here is that you can now feed your Living Ship a Doomed Cream Cake.[/size]
For help with cooking,[url=https://nomanssky.fandom.com/wiki/Cooking] take a look at this wiki page[/url].

name: zCorvette Cockpit Thunderbird v6.24
summary: zCorvette Cockpit Thunderbird Removes the yellow front bumper and the blinking doorway light. Adds headlights to the Thunderbird Cockpit. Now with 500u range! - A Corvette mod.
author: JMZ
description:
[b][u][color=#00ffff][size=5]zCorvette Cockpit Thunderbird v6.24[/size][/color][/u][/b]

[color=#00ffff][size=3]zCorvette Cockpit Thunderbird Removes the yellow front bumper and the blinking doorway light. Adds headlights to the Thunderbird Cockpit. Now with 500u range! - A Corvette mod.[/size][/color]

[size=3]I never liked that [color=#ffff00]yellow pipe[/color] bumper on my Corvette. You could not change the color. What was it protecting me from?
Why is there an annoying blinking light in the doorway?
Flying around the dark side of a planet can be hazardous though. I also like to take a good look at objects of interest before I get out of my ship. So I added [b]headlights[/b]. [u]They have an extended range of 500u enabled by HG's new lighting model.[/u] 

Since all mods are local, only you will see that the bumper is gone and that the headlights are on.
[/size]
[color=#ff7700][size=3][b]Known Issues:[/b][/size][/color]
[size=3]The [b]No Bloom Effect[/b] mod will disable the volumetric effect. The actual lights will work just fine, they just won't look as cool.
This mod is of limited scope, changing only the CockPit_1x2_D.Scene.MBIN, and CockPit_1x2_D_Ext.Scene.MBIN files. This mod will conflict with any other mod that changes this file.
The zCockpit Thunderbird folder should be placed in your No Man’s Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder along with all of your other mods.[/size]

[color=#ffff00][size=3]This mod would not be possible without the use of the fabulous MBINcompiler.[/size][/color]

[color=#00ff00][size=3]I hope you find this mod useful and enjoy it.  If you do like this mod, I ask that you consider taking a moment to endorse it. Endorsements are the only real feedback that is reliable.[/size]

[size=3]Cheers, JMZ[/size][/color]
